newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares fall in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares fall in thin trade.

text.p: The Norwegian stock index edged down in thin turnover on Thursday with the most heavily traded share being a small bank that is the target of a takeover battle.
Oslo's Total index closed 0.27 percent lower at 1,070.57 points in trade worth only 682 million crowns.
About 100 million crowns involved trade in BNbank, a mortgage lender. It fell 1.2 percent to 209 crowns on the news of a new takeover bid by Den norske Bank (DnB).
DnB said it had raised its cash offer for BNbank by 12 crowns to 207 crowns per share including dividend, now valuing BNbank at 1.92 billion crowns excluding dividend.
DnB was unchanged at 27.80 crowns per share.
Fokus Bank, Norway's fourth biggest bank, is bidding for BNbank through a share exchange offer valuing it at 2.06 billion crowns.
